name: Vadodara
short_intro: The cultural capital of Gujarat, shaped by the royal Gaekwad dynasty and its palaces, museums and university.
overview: Vadodara, historically known as Baroda, grew into a refined princely city under the Gaekwads of the Maratha confederacy. It is best known for the vast Laxmi Vilas Palace, the Maharaja Sayajirao University and a thriving arts and music scene. The city blends grand Indo-Saracenic architecture with a relaxed, liveable pace, making it an easy base for exploring central Gujarat.
best_time_to_visit: October to February, when the weather is dry and pleasant. Summers are hot and best avoided.

attractions.name: Laxmi Vilas Palace
attractions.description: A sprawling Indo-Saracenic palace, reputedly several times larger than Buckingham Palace, still home to the royal family.

attractions.name: Sayaji Baug
attractions.description: A large public garden with a zoo, planetarium and a toy train, laid out along the Vishwamitri river.

attractions.name: Maharaja Fateh Singh Museum
attractions.description: Royal art collection including works by Raja Ravi Varma.

attractions.name: Kirti Mandir
attractions.description: The Gaekwad family cenotaph, decorated with murals by Nandalal Bose.

culture.summary: Vadodara is a university town with deep roots in classical music, painting and theatre. The Faculty of Fine Arts has shaped generations of Indian artists.

festivals.name: Navratri
festivals.description: Nine nights of Garba and Dandiya dance, among the most vibrant in Gujarat.
festivals.significance: Devotion to goddess Amba, celebrated with community dance.

festivals.name: Uttarayan (Kite Festival)
festivals.description: The winter kite-flying festival fills the sky over the city.

food.name: Sev Usal
food.description: Spicy white peas curry topped with sev, a Baroda specialty.

food.name: Lilva Kachori
food.description: Kachori stuffed with seasonal pigeon peas.

food.name: Gujarati Thali
food.description: A balanced platter of dals, sabzis, rotli, farsan and sweets.

travel_info.airport: Vadodara Airport (BDQ), ~6 km from the centre.
travel_info.railway: Vadodara Junction, a major stop on the Mumbai–Delhi line.
travel_info.bus: Well connected by state and private buses across Gujarat.
travel_info.local_transport: Autos, app cabs and city buses.
travel_info.budget: Moderate; comfortable mid-range stays and affordable food.

tips: Generally very safe for travellers, including solo visitors.
Carry water and sun protection in summer.
etiquette: Dress modestly at temples and heritage sites.

name: Agra
short_intro: Home of the Taj Mahal and a trio of Mughal World Heritage Sites on the banks of the Yamuna.
overview: Agra was the seat of the Mughal empire at its zenith and preserves three UNESCO World Heritage Sites: the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and nearby Fatehpur Sikri. Beyond the marble mausoleum, the city rewards travellers who linger with riverside views, Mughal gardens and a living tradition of marble inlay craft.
best_time_to_visit: October to March. Visit the Taj at sunrise to avoid crowds and harsh light. Closed on Fridays.

attractions.name: Taj Mahal
attractions.description: The ivory-white marble mausoleum built by Shah Jahan for Mumtaz Mahal, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

attractions.name: Agra Fort
attractions.description: A red-sandstone Mughal fort and palace complex, also a World Heritage Site.

attractions.name: Mehtab Bagh
attractions.description: A riverside Mughal garden offering the classic reflected view of the Taj at sunset.

attractions.name: Itmad-ud-Daulah
attractions.description: The delicate 'Baby Taj', an early marble tomb that influenced the Taj Mahal.

culture.summary: Agra carries a strong Mughal legacy in its cuisine, crafts and Urdu heritage. Marble inlay (pietra dura) is still practised by descendants of the Taj artisans.

festivals.name: Taj Mahotsav
festivals.description: A ten-day arts, crafts and food festival celebrating the region's heritage.

food.name: Agra Petha
food.description: Translucent candied ash-gourd sweet, the city's signature.

food.name: Mughlai Curries
food.description: Rich, slow-cooked kebabs and gravies from the Mughal kitchen.

food.name: Bedai and Jalebi
food.description: Spicy stuffed puri with a sweet jalebi, a classic Agra morning.

travel_info.airport: Agra Airport (AGR); most travellers use Delhi (~230 km).
travel_info.railway: Agra Cantt is well connected; the Gatimaan Express reaches from Delhi in ~100 minutes.
travel_info.bus: Frequent buses on the Yamuna Expressway from Delhi.
travel_info.local_transport: Autos, e-rickshaws and cabs; battery vehicles near the Taj.
travel_info.budget: Moderate; a wide range of stays from budget to luxury.

tips: Beware of unofficial 'guides' and touts around the Taj.
Buy tickets online to skip queues.
safety.emergency: Dial 112; tourist police operate around major monuments.
etiquette: Photography is restricted inside the Taj mausoleum chamber.

name: Spiti Valley
short_intro: A high-altitude cold desert of monasteries, moonscapes and some of the highest villages on earth.
overview: Spiti, meaning 'the middle land', is a remote Trans-Himalayan valley wedged between India and Tibet. Ancient Buddhist monasteries cling to ochre cliffs, glacial rivers cut through barren mountains, and villages like Komic and Hikkim sit above 4,500 metres. It is a demanding, deeply rewarding landscape for travellers seeking silence and scale.

best_time_to_visit: June to September for road access via Manali. The Shimla–Kaza route stays open longer but Kunzum Pass closes in winter.

attractions.name: Key Monastery
attractions.description: The largest monastery in Spiti, a thousand-year-old Buddhist complex above the Spiti river.

attractions.name: Chandratal Lake
attractions.description: A crescent-shaped high-altitude lake near Kunzum Pass, famed for its changing colours.

attractions.name: Langza
attractions.description: A village with a giant Buddha statue and marine fossils from the ancient Tethys sea.

attractions.name: Hikkim
attractions.description: Home to one of the world's highest post offices.

culture.summary: Spiti follows Tibetan Buddhism, with monastic life at the heart of its villages. Homestays offer barley-based food, butter tea and a window into high-desert living.

festivals.name: Losar
festivals.description: Tibetan New Year celebrated with masked dances and prayers.
festivals.significance: Marks renewal and the lunar new year.

festivals.name: Ladarcha Fair
festivals.description: A trade and cultural fair once linking Spiti, Ladakh and Tibet.

food.name: Thukpa
food.description: Warming noodle soup with vegetables or meat.

food.name: Momos
food.description: Steamed dumplings, a Himalayan staple.

food.name: Butter Tea
food.description: Salted tea churned with butter, essential at altitude.

travel_info.airport: Bhuntar (Kullu) is the nearest airport; most reach by road from Manila or Shimla.
travel_info.railway: Nearest railheads are Shimla (narrow gauge) and Chandigarh.
travel_info.bus: HRTC buses run Shimla–Kaza and Manali–Kaza in season.
travel_info.local_transport: Shared taxis and self-drive; a hardy vehicle is recommended.
travel_info.budget: Moderate; homestays keep costs low but travel is time-intensive.

tips: Acclimatise for a day or two to avoid altitude sickness.
Carry cash; ATMs are scarce beyond Kaza.
Fuel up at Kaza, the only reliable pump.
safety.emergency: Dial 112; medical facilities are limited, so carry basic medication.
etiquette: Walk clockwise around monasteries and stupas.
Ask before photographing monks or interiors.

name: Ziro Valley
short_intro: A gentle green valley of paddy fields and pine hills, home of the Apatani tribe and a famous music festival.
overview: Ziro is a wide, undulating valley in Arunachal Pradesh, celebrated for the ingenious wet-rice-and-fish farming of the Apatani people and its UNESCO tentative-list cultural landscape. Pine-clad hills frame emerald paddy fields, and the annual Ziro Festival of Music has made it a favourite with independent travellers.
best_time_to_visit: March to October; late September for the Ziro Festival of Music. Carry an Inner Line Permit.

attractions.name: Apatani Villages
attractions.description: Traditional villages like Hong and Hija with bamboo homes and terraced fields.

attractions.name: Talley Valley Wildlife Sanctuary
attractions.description: A biodiverse reserve of silver fir and clouded-leopard habitat.

attractions.name: Tarin Fish Farm
attractions.description: Showcases the Apatani paddy-cum-pisciculture technique.

attractions.name: Meghna Cave Temple
attractions.description: A hilltop cave shrine with valley views.

culture.summary: The Apatani are known for sustainable agriculture, distinctive facial tattoos among elders, and a strong sense of community governance.

festivals.name: Dree Festival
festivals.description: An agricultural festival praying for a good harvest.

festivals.name: Ziro Festival of Music
festivals.description: An outdoor independent-music festival in the paddy fields.
festivals.significance: Draws artists and travellers from across India.

food.name: Pika Pila
food.description: A tangy fermented pickle of pork fat and bamboo shoot.

food.name: Rice with Fish
food.description: Local rice paired with fish raised in the paddies.

food.name: Apong
food.description: Traditional rice beer served at celebrations.

travel_info.airport: Lilabari (North Lakhimpur, Assam) is nearest; Hollongi (Itanagar) is developing.
travel_info.bus: Shared sumos run from Itanagar and North Lakhimpur.
travel_info.local_transport: Shared taxis; hire a vehicle for village visits.
travel_info.budget: Budget to moderate; homestays are the highlight.

tips: Indian citizens need an Inner Line Permit; foreigners need a Protected Area Permit.
Nights are cold even in summer.
safety.emergency: Dial 112; carry basic medicines as facilities are limited.
etiquette: Respect village customs and sacred groves.

name: Panaji
short_intro: Goa's riverfront capital, where Portuguese-era Latin Quarter lanes meet the Mandovi's cruise boats.
overview: Panaji (Panjim) is the compact, walkable capital of Goa, set where the Mandovi river meets the Arabian Sea. Its Fontainhas Latin Quarter preserves ochre-and-blue Portuguese houses, chapels and bakeries, while nearby Old Goa holds grand cathedrals. It is a calmer, culture-first counterpoint to Goa's beach scene.
best_time_to_visit: November to February for dry, mild weather. The monsoon (June–September) is lush but wet.

attractions.name: Fontainhas Latin Quarter
attractions.description: A colourful old neighbourhood of narrow lanes and Portuguese villas.

attractions.name: Church of Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception
attractions.description: The iconic whitewashed church above Panaji's old market.

attractions.name: Basilica of Bom Jesus (Old Goa)
attractions.description: A UNESCO World Heritage baroque church holding the relics of St. Francis Xavier.

attractions.name: Miramar Beach
attractions.description: A city beach at the mouth of the Mandovi.

culture.summary: Goan culture fuses Konkani and Portuguese influences in its food, music, susegad pace of life and Indo-Portuguese architecture.

festivals.name: Goa Carnival
festivals.description: A colourful pre-Lent street parade with floats and music.
festivals.significance: A Portuguese-era tradition unique in India.

festivals.name: Feast of St. Francis Xavier
festivals.description: A major pilgrimage at Old Goa.

food.name: Goan Fish Curry Rice
food.description: Coconut-and-tamarind fish curry over rice, the everyday classic.

food.name: Pork Vindaloo
food.description: A fiery, tangy Indo-Portuguese pork curry.

food.name: Bebinca
food.description: A layered coconut-and-egg dessert.

travel_info.railway: Karmali is the nearest station; Madgaon is the main junction.
travel_info.bus: Frequent state and interstate buses; Kadamba terminal in Panaji.
travel_info.local_transport: Rented scooters, cabs and app taxis.
travel_info.suggested_duration: 1–2 days in Panaji within a longer Goa trip

tips: Swim only in flagged zones; heed lifeguard warnings.
Prices peak sharply around New Year.
safety.emergency: Dial 112; drishti lifeguards patrol main beaches.

name: Cherrapunji (Sohra)
short_intro: One of the wettest places on earth, famed for living root bridges, plunging waterfalls and misty gorges.
overview: Cherrapunji, known locally as Sohra, sits on the edge of the Khasi Hills where the plateau drops dramatically towards Bangladesh. Monsoon clouds crash into these cliffs, feeding towering waterfalls and the region's unique living root bridges, grown over generations by the Khasi people from the roots of rubber fig trees.
best_time_to_visit: September to April for clearer skies and green valleys. The monsoon is spectacular but roads and treks get slippery.

attractions.name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge
attractions.description: A two-tiered bridge of woven fig roots reached by a steep descent near Nongriat.

attractions.name: Nohkalikai Falls
attractions.description: One of India's tallest plunge waterfalls, dropping into a turquoise pool.

attractions.name: Mawsmai Cave
attractions.description: An illuminated limestone cave easy to walk through.

attractions.name: Seven Sisters Falls
attractions.description: A seven-segmented waterfall best seen after rain.

culture.summary: The Khasi are a matrilineal community. Their bioengineering of living root bridges is a globally rare example of sustainable indigenous knowledge.

festivals.name: Nongkrem Dance Festival
festivals.description: A Khasi thanksgiving festival with ceremonial dance.
festivals.significance: Prays for a good harvest and community wellbeing.

food.name: Jadoh
food.description: Khasi rice cooked with pork and spices.

food.name: Tungrymbai
food.description: Fermented soybean relish.

food.name: Pumaloi
food.description: Steamed powdered-rice cake.

travel_info.airport: Shillong (Umroi) is nearest; Guwahati has the major airport (~150 km).
travel_info.railway: Guwahati is the nearest major railhead.
travel_info.bus: Shared taxis and buses from Shillong (~55 km).
travel_info.local_transport: Hired taxis; treks are on foot.

tips: The Double Decker trek involves thousands of steep steps; carry water and go slow.
Leeches appear in the wet season.
safety.emergency: Dial 112; carry a basic first-aid kit for treks.
etiquette: Do not litter on trails; respect village entry fees and rules.

name: Shillong
short_intro: The 'Scotland of the East', a pine-clad hill capital known for waterfalls, lakes and a live-music culture.
overview: Shillong, the capital of Meghalaya, spreads across rolling pine hills at around 1,500 metres. Colonial-era architecture, clear lakes and a famously strong music scene give the city an easygoing charm. It is the natural gateway to Meghalaya's waterfalls, caves and living root bridges.
best_time_to_visit: October to May for pleasant weather; the monsoon brings heavy rain.

attractions.name: Umiam Lake
attractions.description: A large reservoir with boating and viewpoints north of the city.

attractions.name: Elephant Falls
attractions.description: A tiered waterfall a short drive from Shillong.

attractions.name: Shillong Peak
attractions.description: The highest point, offering panoramic city views.

attractions.name: Ward's Lake
attractions.description: A landscaped garden lake in the city centre.

culture.summary: Shillong blends Khasi traditions with a Western-influenced music culture; it is often called the rock capital of India.

festivals.name: Shillong Cherry Blossom Festival
festivals.description: Celebrates the autumn cherry bloom with music and food.
festivals.significance: A modern festival that draws national artists.

festivals.name: Wangala
festivals.description: The Garo harvest festival of a hundred drums.

food.name: Jadoh
food.description: Khasi pork-and-rice dish.

food.name: Dohneiiong
food.description: Pork cooked with black sesame.

food.name: Momos and Thukpa
food.description: Popular Himalayan street food.

travel_info.bus: Frequent shared taxis and buses from Guwahati.
travel_info.local_transport: Local taxis run on shared routes.

tips: Traffic can be slow; plan waterfall day-trips early.
Carry a light raincoat year-round.
etiquette: Respect local customs; many sites have entry rules.

name: Gangtok
short_intro: Sikkim's clean, cheerful hill capital with Himalayan views, monasteries and a lively pedestrian mall.
overview: Gangtok is the capital of Sikkim, terraced across a Himalayan ridge with views of Kanchenjunga on clear days. Buddhist monasteries, a spotless reputation, a ropeway and the buzzing MG Marg promenade make it one of the most traveller-friendly hill towns in the country and the base for high-altitude excursions.
best_time_to_visit: March to May and October to November for clear mountain views.

attractions.name: MG Marg
attractions.description: A litter-free, vehicle-free boulevard lined with cafes and shops.

attractions.name: Rumtek Monastery
attractions.description: A major seat of Tibetan Buddhism near the city.

attractions.name: Tsomgo (Changu) Lake
attractions.description: A glacial lake at ~3,750 m, reached via a permit.

attractions.name: Ganesh Tok
attractions.description: A hilltop shrine with sweeping valley views.

culture.summary: Sikkim blends Nepali, Bhutia and Lepcha cultures with strong Buddhist traditions and a pioneering organic-farming identity.

festivals.name: Losar
festivals.description: Tibetan New Year with monastery dances.

festivals.name: Saga Dawa
festivals.description: A sacred Buddhist month commemorating the Buddha's life.

food.name: Momos
food.description: Steamed or fried dumplings with dips.

food.name: Thukpa
food.description: Hearty noodle soup.

food.name: Gundruk
food.description: Fermented leafy greens, a Nepali staple.

travel_info.airport: Pakyong (PYG) near Gangtok; Bagdogra is the main regional airport.
travel_info.railway: New Jalpaiguri (NJP) is the nearest major railhead.
travel_info.bus: Shared taxis from NJP/Siliguri are the common route.
travel_info.local_transport: Shared and reserved taxis; the town centre is walkable.

tips: Permits are required for Tsomgo Lake and Nathula.
Book high-altitude trips through registered operators.
etiquette: Sikkim is largely plastic-restricted; carry a reusable bottle.

name: Udaipur
short_intro: The City of Lakes, a Rajput capital of palaces mirrored in shimmering water.
overview: Udaipur, founded by Maharana Udai Singh II in 1559, is the historic capital of Mewar and one of India's most romantic cities. Whitewashed havelis and grand palaces line a chain of interconnected lakes framed by the Aravalli hills, with the vast City Palace and the island Lake Palace as its centrepieces.

images.hero_credit: Geri from Biel/Bienne, Schweiz · CC BY-SA 2.0

best_time_to_visit: October to March; summers are very hot.

attractions.name: City Palace
attractions.description: A sprawling lakeside palace complex of courtyards, museums and balconies.

attractions.name: Lake Pichola
attractions.description: The city's central lake, famous for sunset boat rides.

attractions.name: Jagdish Temple
attractions.description: An ornate 17th-century Vishnu temple in the old city.

attractions.name: Saheliyon Ki Bari
attractions.description: A garden of fountains and lotus pools built for royal ladies.

culture.summary: Udaipur carries a proud Mewar Rajput heritage of miniature painting, folk music and a living palace tradition.

festivals.name: Mewar Festival
festivals.description: Celebrates the arrival of spring with processions and folk performances.
festivals.significance: Tied to the Gangaur festival honouring goddess Parvati.

festivals.name: Shilpgram Utsav
festivals.description: A crafts and performing-arts fair on the city's edge.

food.name: Dal Baati Churma
food.description: Baked wheat balls with lentils and a sweet crumble.

food.name: Gatte ki Sabzi
food.description: Gram-flour dumplings in a spiced yoghurt curry.

food.name: Mawa Kachori
food.description: A rich fried pastry filled with sweetened khoya.

travel_info.railway: Udaipur City station is well connected.
travel_info.bus: Good bus links across Rajasthan and to Gujarat.
travel_info.local_transport: Autos and cabs; the old city is best explored on foot.
travel_info.budget: Moderate to premium; iconic heritage hotels available.

tips: Agree on auto fares in advance.
Old-city lanes are narrow; watch for scooters.
safety.emergency: Dial 112; tourist police present at major sites.
etiquette: Cover shoulders and knees at temples.

name: Rishikesh
short_intro: The yoga capital of the world, where the Ganga leaves the Himalaya amid ashrams and white-water rapids.
overview: Rishikesh sits where the Ganga emerges from the mountains onto the plains, a town of ashrams, riverside temples and the famous Lakshman Jhula and Ram Jhula suspension bridges. It is simultaneously a centre of yoga and meditation and India's white-water rafting hub, giving it a rare blend of the spiritual and the adventurous.
best_time_to_visit: September to April; rafting season peaks in autumn and spring. Summer is warm and the monsoon swells the river.

attractions.name: Triveni Ghat
attractions.description: The main riverside ghat, famous for the evening Ganga Aarti.

attractions.name: Lakshman Jhula & Ram Jhula
attractions.description: Iconic suspension footbridges over the Ganga.

attractions.name: The Beatles Ashram
attractions.description: The atmospheric ruins of Maharishi Mahesh Yogi's ashram, covered in murals.

attractions.name: Neelkanth Mahadev Temple
attractions.description: A hill Shiva temple set in forest above the town.

culture.summary: Rishikesh is a vegetarian, alcohol-free spiritual town where yoga, Ayurveda and Ganga worship shape daily rhythms.

festivals.name: International Yoga Festival
festivals.description: A week of yoga, workshops and talks drawing practitioners worldwide.

festivals.name: Ganga Dussehra
festivals.description: Celebrates the descent of the Ganga.

food.name: Sattvic Thali
food.description: Simple vegetarian meals served in ashrams and cafes.

food.name: Aloo Puri
food.description: A popular fried breakfast at riverside stalls.

food.name: Herbal & Ayurvedic Teas
food.description: Widely served in the cafe scene.

travel_info.bus: Frequent buses from Delhi, Dehradun and Haridwar.
travel_info.budget: Budget to moderate; retreats can be premium.

tips: Raft only with licensed operators and wear the provided gear.
River currents are strong; do not swim unsupervised.
etiquette: Alcohol and non-veg food are prohibited in the core town.
Dress modestly near temples and ghats.

name: Hampi
short_intro: A surreal UNESCO landscape of boulder hills and the ruined splendour of the Vijayanagara empire.
overview: Hampi was the capital of the Vijayanagara empire and, in the 16th century, one of the largest and richest cities in the world. Today its temples, bazaars, aqueducts and royal enclosures lie scattered across a dramatic landscape of giant granite boulders beside the Tungabhadra river, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that feels both ancient and otherworldly.
best_time_to_visit: October to February; the Deccan summer is punishing.

attractions.name: Virupaksha Temple
attractions.description: A living temple with a towering gopuram, active since the 7th century.

attractions.name: Vittala Temple & Stone Chariot
attractions.description: Famous for its musical pillars and the iconic stone chariot.

attractions.name: Hemakuta Hill
attractions.description: A cluster of shrines with the best sunset views.

attractions.name: Royal Enclosure
attractions.description: Palace platforms, stepped tanks and the elephant stables.

culture.summary: Hampi preserves Vijayanagara temple architecture and art, and the surrounding Hampi bazaar retains a pilgrimage and backpacker culture.

festivals.name: Hampi Utsav
festivals.description: A state cultural festival with music, dance and light shows amid the ruins.

food.name: North Karnataka Thali
food.description: Jowar roti, spicy curries and chutneys.

food.name: Cafe Fare
food.description: Backpacker cafes across the river serve global comfort food.

travel_info.airport: Hubballi (HBX) or Vidyanagar (Toranagallu); Bengaluru for wider links.
travel_info.bus: Regular buses from Hosapete and Bengaluru.

tips: Carry water and sun protection; ruins have little shade.
Alcohol is restricted on the temple-town side.
etiquette: Do not climb on carvings; respect active temples.

name: Munnar
short_intro: Rolling tea gardens, misty peaks and cool Western Ghats air at the meeting of three mountain streams.
overview: Munnar is a high-range hill station in Kerala's Idukki district, blanketed in emerald tea estates first planted by the British. Set among some of South India's highest peaks, it offers cool weather, waterfalls, spice gardens and the rare Neelakurinji bloom that colours the hills purple once every twelve years.
best_time_to_visit: September to March for clear, cool weather.

attractions.name: Eravikulam National Park
attractions.description: Home to the endangered Nilgiri tahr and rolling grasslands.

attractions.name: Tea Gardens & Tea Museum
attractions.description: Sprawling estates and a museum tracing Munnar's tea history.

attractions.name: Mattupetty Dam
attractions.description: A scenic reservoir with boating.

attractions.name: Top Station
attractions.description: A high viewpoint over the Western Ghats and Tamil Nadu plains.

culture.summary: Munnar's culture is shaped by its plantation history and a mix of Tamil estate-worker and Malayali communities.

festivals.name: Neelakurinji Bloom
festivals.description: The hills turn purple as the Neelakurinji flowers en masse.
festivals.significance: A rare natural spectacle, last in 2018.

food.name: Kerala Sadya
food.description: A vegetarian feast served on a banana leaf.

food.name: Appam with Stew
food.description: Lacy rice pancakes with coconut-milk stew.

food.name: Fresh Cardamom Tea
food.description: Estate-fresh spiced tea.

travel_info.railway: Aluva or Ernakulam are the nearest railheads.
travel_info.bus: Regular buses from Kochi, Madurai and Munnar KSRTC.
travel_info.local_transport: Taxis and jeeps for estate and viewpoint tours.

tips: Mountain roads are winding; avoid night driving.
Carry a light layer; evenings are cold.
etiquette: Stick to marked trails inside the national park.
